(Today through Friday)...
Issued at 217 AM EST Sat Nov 28 2026

Early This Morning through Today...

Brief upper ridging has allowed for a clear slot in the clouds to 
move across central Indiana early this morning. However, some 
patchy stratus was forming in this slot. Mid and high clouds from 
the next system were already moving in from the west.

Winds remaining up should keep fog at bay in the clear area, but 
patchy stratus will continue during the night. Mid and high clouds 
will continue to increase across the area as lift with a jet streak 
and weak upper trough move in. 

Lift will be mainly confined to the mid levels, with limited 
moisture in the lower levels. While some hi-res short term guidance 
is showing light precipitation moving in before sunrise and moving 
east through the morning, believe this is overdone as best forcing 
will be north of the area and the limited moisture in the lower 
levels. Will go with a dry forecast for now, but will watch for the 
need to add any sprinkles/flurries.

Clouds will briefly decrease behind this first system, but they will 
increase again this afternoon ahead of the next, stronger system. 
Still, there will be enough sunshine to boost temperatures into the 
middle 40s to around 50 for highs.

Tonight through Sunday Night...

A strengthening upper trough and jet stream will deepen a surface low 
pressure system that will move through the area on Sunday. 
Relatively strong winds with this system will transport good 
moisture into the area. The broad forcing with this system will 
work with the moisture to produce widespread showers at times Sunday 
into Sunday evening.

Initial warm advection ahead of the system may bring some rain 
overnight, so will have some mainly chance PoPs then. Will go 
categorical PoPs Sunday into Sunday evening, with PoPs diminishing 
to dry Sunday night from west to east.

Some weak instability will sneak into the far southern forecast area 
just south of the surface low, so will have a mention of thunder 
there. Severe storms are not expected with better instability 
remaining south of central Indiana.

The system will have good frontogenetical forcing with it. General 
rainfall amounts of a half to three quarters of an inch are 
expected, but the frontogenetical forcing will lead to banded 
heavier rain which could bring local amounts over an inch.

Some of the strong wind field with the system (50kt at 850mb on 
the cold side) will mix down in cold advection later Sunday into 
Sunday night, creating gusty conditions. Wind gusts to 35 mph are 
expected, with at least some potential for higher gusts.

Thickening clouds will help keep low temperatures in the middle and 
upper 30s tonight, so only rain is expected. Highs on Sunday will 
depend in part on the path of the surface low, but for now have gone 
with mid 40s north to mid 50s south. While low temperatures Sunday 
night will be in the 20s to lower 30s, precipitation will have 
exited the area before readings get cold enough for snow.

Monday through Wednesday...

A weak upper system will move through nearly zonal flow aloft around 
Tuesday, but forcing/moisture will be limited. Will go with a dry 
forecast during this period with surface high pressure in control 
for much of the time.

Monday will be cool behind the stronger system, but readings will 
moderate by Wednesday as southerly flow sets up on the west side of 
high pressure. Highs on Wednesday will be in the 50s.

Thursday and beyond...

A stronger upper system with an associated surface low pressure 
system will move through around Friday, bringing rain chances from 
Thursday to Saturday. Highest PoPs are expected to be on Friday, but 
some uncertainty remains in the timing of the system. 

Highs will warm into the 60s for Thursday and Friday, but they will 
cool back into the 50s for Saturday.
